newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARTWALL SEES CLEARLY BETTER 1996 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: HARTWALL SEES CLEARLY BETTER 1996 PROFIT.

text.p: Finnish beverages group Oy Hartwall Ab said on Thursday it expected full-year 1996 pre-tax profit to be clearly better than last year's 45 million markka.

"We expect the result before appropriations and taxes for the full year to remain clearly better than the corresponding result last year," Hartwall said in a statement with its January-August results.
The group's eight-month profit after financial items surged 230 percent to nearly 140 million markka.

Hartwall attributed the rise in profits to good performances by its domestic operations and by Baltic Beverages Holding AB, a 50-percent owned subsidiary, and to the fact that last year's result was burdened by heavy extraordinary restructuring costs.

Group net sales increased 10.6 percent to 1.34 billion markka in January-August with sales in Finland down 1.8 percent at 1.01 billion markka but sales in the Baltic republics and Russia increasing 94 percent to 293 million markka.
The volume of Hartwall's eight-month sales rose 7.3 percent to 380 million litres, the company said.
